name: Web Service

evidence.rationale: An application-aware or destination-restricted endpoint firewall can block unauthorized web, cloud, file-sharing, or social-media services used for command and control.

CIS 9.3 helps prevent link-based and web-based initial access by stopping users from reaching malicious or unapproved content in the first place. It does this by requiring updated network-based URL filtering across all enterprise assets, using methods such as category-based filtering, reputation-based filtering, and block lists. In practice, this means enforcing controls that restrict access to unsafe websites, malicious downloads, risky scripts, and unauthorized browser extensions, reducing the risk of phishing, exploitation, and malware delivery. If 9.3 implementation includes certain risky or suspicious web-services used broadly enough to block unauthorized services, then this technique is applicable.

Adversaries use external Web services as command-and-control infrastructure. Dedicated administrative systems have no direct Internet access, directly preventing them from establishing command-and-control sessions with external Web services.
Network intrusion prevention solutions can use signatures for known adversary malware to block identifiable command-and-control traffic using web services.
Web proxies and application-layer gateways can restrict access to unauthorized external web services, limiting their use for adversary command and control.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.

ATLAS results describe the ATLAS release in versions.atlas, pinned by commit and digest. ATLAS changes often: a later release can add techniques and mitigations. An empty mitigation list means that this release links no mitigation, not that no mitigation exists. agent_related is derived by this project from names.
